pr.title: Run each draft-state and publish command on a line by itself
pr.head: 95aff4afec3aacf41fdab35521f143eacaf62058

summary: Projector's skills tell agents to move a pull request's draft state with project review hold and project review ready, and to post a review with project review publish. project init adds the allow rule Bash(project *) to the user's Claude Code settings, and matching prefix rules to their Codex rules, so these commands run without a prompt and without the host's automatic approval judging them.

That rule decides a call only when every command in it matches a rule. Claude Code and Codex check each command of a chain, such as one joined with &&, and take the strictest result. So a gh pr view joined to project review ready sent the whole call to auto mode, which refused it as undoing a hold. The skill then told the agent to stop and ask the user, so the pull request stayed a draft.

This change tells the agent to run each of the three commands as a tool call of its own, not after cd and joined to nothing. When the host refuses one, the agent tells a joined call from a missing rule, as summarize-pr already does for project summary publish after #446, which this branch merged. A new test fails when any skill's shell example joins one of the three commands to another command.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Hold. project review hold converts a signed-off pull request to a draft while its author builds a change on it, so nobody merges it meanwhile.
  • Allow rule. A Claude Code permission rule, such as Bash(project *), or a Codex prefix rule, that lets a command run without a prompt.
  • Auto mode. Claude Code's automatic approval, which judges commands no rule decides and can refuse them.
  • project review rules --json. Reports, for each host's settings file, whether it holds every rule project init writes (allowed) and whether it allows project summary publish (summary_publish). It writes nothing.

groups.title: Why a joined call loses the allow rule
groups.kicker: The full rule, its reason, and the refusal steps, in the skill that holds pull requests
intro: fix-pr fixes review findings on a pull request. When a clean pull request needs a change, it holds the pull request as a draft, pushes the change, and marks it ready again. This group rewrites the passage on those two commands.

The passage now says that each command prints the draft state and the head it acted on, so no gh pr view is needed after it. It says to run each command as a tool call of its own, and why a chained call falls to automatic approval. It then gives two steps for a refusal:

1. The call ran more than the command. Run the command again, alone.
  2. The command ran alone. Read allowed in project review rules --json. Send the user to project init when it is false or the file is not listed. When it is true, ask the user to run the command themselves.

files.note: The passage under "Hold the pull request while changes are built" that says how to run hold and ready, and what to do when the host refuses one.

checks.text: Each command prints the head. set_draft in src/projector/review.py returns the head it read after the change, and draft_lines prints it, as in marked ninjudd/projector#463 ready for review at c951842.

The rule project init adds is Bash(project *), as the text says: ALLOW in src/projector/permissions.py. Its Codex prefix rules include review hold, ready, and publish. Both commands act on --repo from any directory, so the rule against a cd leaves them runnable.
Running the command again alone is the same command, not another form of it. A command refused while alone still goes to the user, never to gh pr ready.

Each file's allowed in review_rules is true only when init would leave that file unchanged, and the Codex file is listed only where Codex is installed. So false or a missing file is the case init fixes.

groups.title: The skills that point at the rule
groups.kicker: Three skills repeat the rule where they mark ready or publish
intro: implement and spec mark a pull request ready at the hand-over, and review-pr publishes a review. Each now says to run its command as a tool call of its own, not after cd and joined to no other command, and points at fix-pr for the reason.
review-pr also follows fix-pr's refusal steps for a refused publish. It runs the publish again alone after a joined call, and reads allowed before it asks the user to run project init.

groups.title: Tests that keep the rule in the skills
groups.kicker: Skill text and shell examples checked for joined commands
intro: test_the_skills_move_draft_state_through_the_commands_alone now checks that fix-pr, implement, and spec say "as a tool call of its own". It also checks that fix-pr carries both refusal steps.

test_no_skill_example_joins_a_review_command_to_another reads every fenced sh or bash block in every skill. It fails on a line that runs project review ready, hold, or publish beside ;, &&, or a pipe. It strips <…> placeholders first, so <clean|changes-requested> is not read as a pipe.

checks.text: The new test catches the bug it names. With && gh pr view <number> appended to the project review ready example in a copy of fix-pr at this head, it fails on &&.
